title: Aria in C (Op. 42, Lesson 2)
about: A simple C-major aria from Clementi's 1801 piano method, Introduction to the Art of Playing on the Piano Forte, Op. 42.

title: Ah, vous dirai-je, maman (Op. 42, Lesson 18)
about: The French folk tune known in English as "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star", set as an easy lesson in Clementi's Op. 42 method (1801).

title: Moderato after Mozart (Op. 42, Lesson 1)
about: The very first lesson piece in Clementi's 1801 piano method, a short Moderato drawn from a melody by Mozart.

title: Air after Handel (Op. 42, Lesson 3)
about: A short air by Handel, simplified by Clementi as an early lesson in his Op. 42 piano method (1801).

title: In May
about: A short, cheerful teaching piece by Franz Behr, a 19th-century German composer of many pieces for young pianists.

title: Air in D minor, BWV Anh. 131
about: A tiny two-voice air from the 1725 Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach.

title: Eight-Measure Exercise No. 1, Op. 821
about: The first of Czerny's 160 Eight-Measure Exercises, Op. 821 — a compact study in even right-hand fingerwork.

title: Aria "So oft ich meine Tabakspfeife", BWV 515
about: A short song tune from the 1725 Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach, here as a simple two-part keyboard piece.

title: Eight-Measure Exercise No. 5, Op. 821
about: A brief study from Czerny's 160 Eight-Measure Exercises, Op. 821, working on evenness between the hands.

title: Arietta after Mozart (Op. 42, Lesson 12)
about: A graceful 6/8 arietta by Mozart arranged as a lesson in Clementi's 1801 piano method.

title: Air "Fal lal la" (Op. 42, Lesson 20)
about: A popular English air of the day, arranged by Clementi as a lesson in his Op. 42 method (1801).

title: Minuet in F, K. 2
about: One of Mozart's first compositions, written in 1762 when he was six years old.

title: Minuet in F, BWV Anh. 113
about: A simple minuet from the 1725 Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach.

title: Melody, Op. 68 No. 1
about: The opening piece of Schumann's Album for the Young (1848): a singing melody over a flowing left hand.

title: Humming Song, Op. 68 No. 3
about: A gentle lullaby-like piece from Schumann's Album for the Young (1848).

title: Chorale, Op. 68 No. 4
about: A hymn-style chorale harmonisation from Schumann's Album for the Young (1848).

title: Little Piece, Op. 68 No. 5
about: A short piece from Schumann's Album for the Young (1848) in which the melody passes between the hands.

title: Les étoiles d'or No. 1: Valse
about: An easy salon waltz by Jean-Louis Gobbaerts, who wrote many teaching pieces under the pen name Streabbog.

title: The Harebell
about: A light teaching piece by William Smallwood, the English author of a famous 19th-century piano tutor.

title: Theme after Pleyel (Op. 42, Lesson 23)
about: A short theme by Ignaz Pleyel, arranged by Clementi as a lesson in his Op. 42 piano method (1801).

title: Minuet in G, BWV Anh. 114
about: The famous Minuet in G from the 1725 Anna Magdalena Notebook, now usually credited to Christian Petzold.

title: Minuet in G minor, BWV Anh. 115
about: The G-minor companion to the famous Minuet in G from the 1725 Anna Magdalena Notebook, now usually credited to Christian Petzold.

title: Minuet in A minor, BWV Anh. 120
about: A short minor-key minuet from the 1725 Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach.

title: Morning Prayer, Op. 39 No. 1
about: The chorale-like opening piece of Tchaikovsky's Children's Album (1878).

title: Old French Song, Op. 39 No. 16
about: A wistful melody from Tchaikovsky's Children's Album (1878).

title: Soldiers' March, Op. 68 No. 2
about: A crisp march from Schumann's Album for the Young (1848).

title: The Happy Farmer, Op. 68 No. 10
about: One of the best-known pieces in Schumann's Album for the Young (1848), with the tune in the left hand.

title: La Candeur (Frankness), Op. 100 No. 1
about: The first of Burgmüller's 25 Easy and Progressive Studies, Op. 100 (1851): a singing melody over a flowing left hand.

title: Innocence, Op. 100 No. 5
about: A graceful little waltz-study from Burgmüller's 25 Easy and Progressive Studies, Op. 100 (1851).

title: Progrès (Progress), Op. 100 No. 6
about: A study in scales and broken thirds from Burgmüller's 25 Easy and Progressive Studies, Op. 100 (1851).

title: Applicatio, BWV 994
about: A tiny piece from the 1720 Clavier-Büchlein for Wilhelm Friedemann Bach, with fingerings written by Bach himself.

title: Musette in D, BWV Anh. 126
about: A bagpipe-like dance with a drone bass from the 1725 Anna Magdalena Notebook.

title: March in E-flat, BWV Anh. 127
about: A stately march from the 1725 Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach.

title: The Wild Rider, Op. 68 No. 8
about: A galloping minor-key piece from Schumann's Album for the Young (1848), with the tune passing between the hands.

title: First Loss, Op. 68 No. 16
about: A short, sorrowful piece from Schumann's Album for the Young (1848).

title: March of the Wooden Soldiers, Op. 39 No. 5
about: A toy-soldier march from Tchaikovsky's Children's Album (1878).

title: L'Arabesque, Op. 100 No. 2
about: A lively study in quick five-note figures from Burgmüller's Op. 100 (1851).

title: La Pastorale, Op. 100 No. 3
about: A gentle 6/8 pastoral study with turns, from Burgmüller's Op. 100 (1851).

title: Tendre Fleur (Tender Flower), Op. 100 No. 10
about: A delicate study in two-note slurs and chords from Burgmüller's Op. 100 (1851).

title: Sonatina in C, Op. 36 No. 1: I. Allegro
about: The first movement of Clementi's best-known teaching sonatina, published in 1797.

title: Sonatina in C, Op. 36 No. 1: III. Vivace
about: The bright 3/8 finale of Clementi's Sonatina Op. 36 No. 1 (1797).

title: Sonatina in B-flat, HWV 585
about: A short two-part Baroque sonatina by Handel, often used to introduce contrapuntal playing.

title: Ballade, Op. 100 No. 15
about: A dramatic minor-key study with a left-hand melody, from Burgmüller's Op. 100 (1851).

title: La Chasse (The Hunt), Op. 100 No. 9
about: A brisk hunting piece with horn-call figures, from Burgmüller's Op. 100 (1851).

title: Sonatina in C, Op. 20 No. 1: I. Allegro
about: The opening movement of Kuhlau's popular teaching Sonatina Op. 20 No. 1 (1820).

title: Little Prelude in D minor, BWV 926
about: A broken-chord prelude from the 1720 Clavier-Büchlein for Wilhelm Friedemann Bach.

title: Little Prelude in F, BWV 928
about: A cheerful two-part prelude from the 1720 Clavier-Büchlein for Wilhelm Friedemann Bach.

title: Gymnopédie No. 1
about: The first of Satie's three slow, dreamy Gymnopédies, composed in 1888.

title: Of Foreign Lands and Peoples, Op. 15 No. 1
about: The opening piece of Schumann's Scenes from Childhood (1838), with a melody over gently flowing triplets.

title: Prelude in A, Op. 28 No. 7
about: A brief mazurka-like prelude from Chopin's 24 Preludes, Op. 28 (1839).

title: Åse's Death, Op. 46 No. 2
about: Grieg's own piano version of the slow lament from his Peer Gynt music (1875).

title: Gnossienne No. 1
about: The first of Satie's Gnossiennes (1890), written without bar lines and with an exotic, modal melody.

title: Träumerei, Op. 15 No. 7
about: The famous "Dreaming" from Schumann's Scenes from Childhood (1838).

title: Prelude in E minor, Op. 28 No. 4
about: A slow, melancholy prelude from Chopin's 24 Preludes, Op. 28 (1839), played at his funeral.

title: Prelude in B minor, Op. 28 No. 6
about: A prelude from Chopin's Op. 28 (1839) with the melody in the left hand under repeated right-hand chords.

title: Prelude in C minor, Op. 28 No. 20
about: A solemn, chordal prelude from Chopin's 24 Preludes, Op. 28 (1839).

title: Sonata in G, Op. 49 No. 2: II. Tempo di Menuetto
about: The minuet finale of one of Beethoven's two "easy sonatas" Op. 49, composed in the 1790s.

title: Sonatina in C, Op. 20 No. 1: III. Rondo
about: The lively rondo finale of Kuhlau's Sonatina Op. 20 No. 1 (1820).

title: Sonata in G, Hob. XVI:27: II. Menuetto
about: The minuet and trio from Haydn's Keyboard Sonata in G major, Hob. XVI:27 (c. 1776).

title: Knecht Ruprecht, Op. 68 No. 12
about: A stormy portrait of St. Nicholas's fearsome companion from Schumann's Album for the Young (1848).

title: Invention No. 1 in C, BWV 772
about: The first of Bach's fifteen Two-Part Inventions (1723), built entirely from one short motif.

title: Invention No. 8 in F, BWV 779
about: A bright canonic Two-Part Invention by Bach (1723) in which the hands chase each other.

title: Invention No. 13 in A minor, BWV 784
about: A Two-Part Invention by Bach (1723) built on broken-chord figures.

title: Prelude in C, BWV 846 (Well-Tempered Clavier I)
about: The opening prelude of Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I (1722), made entirely of flowing broken chords.

title: Sonata in C, K. 545: I. Allegro
about: The first movement of Mozart's "Sonata facile", written in 1788 "for beginners".

title: Für Elise, WoO 59
about: Beethoven's famous Bagatelle in A minor (1810), complete with its contrasting middle sections.

title: The Entertainer

title: Venetian Gondola Song, Op. 19 No. 6
about: A rocking barcarolle from Mendelssohn's first book of Songs without Words (1830).

title: Prelude in D-flat, Op. 28 No. 15 "Raindrop"
about: The longest of Chopin's 24 Preludes (1839), named for its persistent repeated note.

title: Nocturne in E minor, Op. 72 No. 1
about: An early nocturne Chopin wrote around 1827, published after his death.

title: Waltz in B minor, Op. 69 No. 2
about: A melancholy early waltz by Chopin (1829), published posthumously.

title: Nocturne in E-flat, Op. 9 No. 2
about: Chopin's most famous nocturne, published in 1832.

title: Sonata in A, K. 331: III. Rondo alla Turca
about: The famous "Turkish March" finale of Mozart's Piano Sonata K. 331 (c. 1783).

title: Fantasia in D minor, K. 397
about: An improvisatory fantasia Mozart wrote in 1782, left unfinished and completed by an unknown hand.

title: Sonata "Pathétique", Op. 13: II. Adagio cantabile
about: The lyrical slow movement of Beethoven's "Pathétique" Sonata (1798).

title: Prelude in C minor, BWV 847 (Well-Tempered Clavier I)
about: A driving 16th-note prelude from Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I (1722).

title: In the Hall of the Mountain King, Op. 46 No. 4
about: Grieg's own piano version of the famous accelerating march from his Peer Gynt music (1875).

title: Sonata "Moonlight", Op. 27 No. 2: I. Adagio sostenuto
about: The hushed, famous first movement of Beethoven's "Moonlight" Sonata (1801).

title: Arabesque No. 1
about: The first of Debussy's two early Arabesques (1888–91), full of flowing triplet figures.

title: Clair de lune (Suite bergamasque)
about: The third movement of Debussy's Suite bergamasque (c. 1890, published 1905).

title: Maple Leaf Rag
about: Scott Joplin's landmark rag of 1899, the best-selling ragtime piece of its era.

title: Waltz in D-flat, Op. 64 No. 1 "Minute"
about: Chopin's whirling "Minute Waltz" (1847).

title: Sonata "Pathétique", Op. 13: III. Rondo
about: The urgent C-minor rondo finale of Beethoven's "Pathétique" Sonata (1798).

title: Impromptu in G-flat, D. 899 No. 3
about: A serene song-like impromptu over rippling accompaniment, from Schubert's Impromptus D. 899 (1827).

title: Consolation No. 3 in D-flat, S. 172

title: Wedding Day at Troldhaugen, Op. 65 No. 6
about: Grieg's festive Lyric Piece of 1896, written for his 25th wedding anniversary.

title: Impromptu in A-flat, D. 935 No. 2
about: A gentle minuet-like impromptu from Schubert's second set of Impromptus, D. 935 (1827).

title: Prelude in C-sharp minor, Op. 3 No. 2
about: Rachmaninoff's famous bell-like prelude, composed in 1892 when he was nineteen.

title: Impromptu in E-flat, D. 899 No. 2
about: A brilliant impromptu of rippling right-hand triplets from Schubert's D. 899 set (1827).

title: Fantaisie-Impromptu, Op. 66
about: Chopin's virtuosic impromptu in C-sharp minor (1834), published after his death.

title: Étude in C minor, Op. 10 No. 12 "Revolutionary"
about: Chopin's stormy left-hand étude, written around 1831.

title: Étude in A-flat, Op. 25 No. 1 "Aeolian Harp"
about: A shimmering arpeggio étude from Chopin's Op. 25 set (published 1837).
